newsitem.title: UK: UK plans new Treasury team to streamline PFI.
newsitem.headline: UK plans new Treasury team to streamline PFI.

text.p: The government said on Monday it would appoint a new Treasury team charged with reviving the ailing Private Finance Initiative.
Paymaster General Geoffrey Robinson said the new 7-9 strong Private Finance Taskforce would "road-test significant projects for their commercial viability before procurement begins."
He told a news conference the body, to run for two years, would also develop skills in other government departments for dealing with PFI projects.
Launched in 1992, the previous Conservative government set up PFI in a bid to get the private sector involved in major public projects such as hospitals, transport schemes and prisons.
Projects valued at just under seven billion stg have been signed or carried out since then, with almost half that figure accounted for by the new rail link from London to the Channel Tunnel.
Labour has accepted the idea of the PFI, and the Conservatives' target of 10 billion stg of projects over the next three years.
But it believes the Initiative's potential has been undermined because projects have not been properly considered before being put out to tender.
After taking office last month, asked Malcolm Bates, a senior executive at Pearl Insurance, to look at how it is operating.
"PFI procurement has been plagued by inefficiencies," Bates said in a summary of his report to the government.
"The current practice of the Treasury becoming involved too late in the process has inevitably led to frustration and increased costs."
Robinson announced the government accepted Bates' report, and would therefore scrap the Private Finance Panel, and replace it with the new body.

Among the recommendations proposed by Bates is one that contractors' bidding costs should be refunded when the government rejects a project, for reasons not related to the viability of tenders received.
Robinson said the government would look sympathetically at this idea. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
